payload.name: Extract Explicit Evaluations with Stated Reasons
payload.description: Use during extraction when a speaker explicitly praises or evaluates another person's role, abilities, or character and gives specific qualities or reasons for that evaluation.
content: When a speaker explicitly states a positive evaluation of someone (e.g., calling them a perfect mentor, great leader, etc.) and provides specific supporting qualities or reasons, create a durable memory candidate that captures the subject, the evaluation, and the exact stated reasons.
Do not merge these specific reasons only into a generic encouragement or support event; keep them as an explicit part of the evaluation so the reason remains answerable.
Stop after recording the evaluation and the stated reasons; do not infer additional qualities or reasons that were not mentioned.

solves: When a speaker gives an explicit positive evaluation of another person's role or character (e.g., calling them a perfect mentor) and states specific reasons or qualities, extraction often captures only the generic encouragement and drops the decisive attributes. This makes later questions about why the speaker holds that opinion unanswerable from memory.
